data.title: How much did the extra trees buy?
data.heading: Illustrative test accuracy by forest size
data.prompt: how does test accuracy change with 1, 5, 10, 50 and 200 trees in a random forest?
data.instructions: Visit each forest size. Compare the last jump with the early jumps; only five settings were supplied.
calculations: Use only the five supplied illustrative (tree count, accuracy) observations; the horizontal axis is logarithmic.
Accuracy percent = source accuracy × 100. Gain in percentage points = (new accuracy − previous accuracy) × 100.
Gain per added tree = gain in percentage points / (new count − previous count). The last interval adds 150 trees for 0.5 pp, or 1/300 pp per added tree.
The connecting line is a guide between observations, not additional measured forest sizes.
